description: Executable unit coverage for the CAPI protocol data, register and lifecycle modules of the AFU control block.

dependency_modules.01_capi_integration/accelerator_rtl/afu_: owned by the parity family, elaborated only as a DUT dependency
owned by the storage family, elaborated only as a DUT dependency

sampling_contract.cycle: a cycle is the interval closed by the posedge that samples it, stimulus is applied on the preceding negedge
sampling_contract.read_data_parity: the doubleword data parity of a buffer write beat is accepted with that beat, afu_control latches valid, tag, tag parity, address, data and data parity of one beat with a single common delay
sampling_contract.read_data_publication: a stored half becomes visible to a response lookup at beat+3, a qualified response publishes half 0 at response+2 and half 1 at response+3, the parity report follows the beat at beat+4
sampling_contract.write_data_publication: a compute unit beat is visible to a buffer read at beat+2, a buffer read returns data and parity at request+3 which equals the published read latency, the tag parity report follows at request+4
sampling_contract.mmio_publication: the selected read data is formed at request+4 from the status inputs sampled at request+2, configuration and acknowledge pulses reach the outputs at request+5, acknowledge, data, data parity and the parity report reach the outputs at request+6
sampling_contract.job_publication: a job command is decoded at command+2, the parity report follows at command+5, the done pulse follows the internal reset release edge and publishes the reported error word in the same cycle
sampling_contract.lifecycle_publication: outputs published in a cycle are produced by the state and inputs of the previous cycle, state advances only while the block is enabled
sampling_contract.read_data_enable: a beat is accepted only while the block is enabled, so tag, address, data and parity of an accepted beat freeze together for the whole disabled window and the parity of that beat keeps being reported against its own parity byte

read-data.independent_model: tag indexed half-association scoreboard with byte level payload storage and a bit counting parity reference
scenarios: lower half first and upper half first for the same tag
half gaps of zero, one and eight cycles
lower half only and upper half only
interleaved halves for four tags with reordered responses
command types outside read and descriptor are not stored
response classes read, descriptor, both, write only, NLOCK, flags without valid and an illegal response code
tag parity fault, data parity fault and both faults
response exactly at the commit boundary and one cycle before it
buffer beats while the block is disabled
asynchronous reset with a drained pipeline and a response that still reads the retained store
a clean beat followed by a corrupted parity byte and a beat that carries a corrupted parity, both only counted when the two parity bytes differ
the enable falls in the cycle after a beat is accepted while the bus keeps presenting a payload whose lane parity differs, for a clean beat and for a beat that carries a parity fault

write-data.independent_model: tag indexed half line memory with an address and lane mask model and a bit counting parity reference
scenarios: store both halves and return each half with its doubleword parity
buffer read at the commit boundary and one cycle before it
buffer read addresses outside the two halves hold the previous data
isolated doubleword lane sweep across all eight lanes
four tags stored and returned in reverse order
only the lower half or only the upper half valid
back to back buffer reads and reads separated by one and eight cycles
a compute unit store concurrent with a buffer read of another tag
tag parity fault and clean tag parity
buffer reads while the block is disabled
asynchronous reset publishes the reset data, parity and latency contract

wed.independent_model: byte level 128 byte descriptor decoder driven from a field group table plus a fetch-once lifecycle model
scenarios: one 128 byte fetch with a byte index pattern that proves the byte order of every field group
lower half first, upper half first, both halves in one cycle and lower half only
requests blocked by the almost full command buffer, by the disable and by both
responses with a foreign engine identifier or a non-done code do not complete the fetch
data halves with a foreign engine identifier are ignored
the descriptor is decoded once and no second command is issued while the request is valid
repeat jobs after an asynchronous reset with a new address and new descriptor bytes
asynchronous reset while idle, while waiting for the response and while publishing
every command payload field is compared as a whole image from the reset state onwards

mmio.independent_model: register and descriptor map written from the documented address map with pulse semantics for configuration and acknowledge registers
scenarios: every mapped status and statistics register is read and compared against the sampled source
every AFU descriptor word plus an unmapped descriptor index, in doubleword, high word and low word modes
every mapped configuration register written with all ones, all zeros and a mixed pattern
acknowledge registers with a set and a zero payload
unmapped read and write accesses
address parity fault, data parity fault and both faults
back to back requests and requests separated by one and twelve cycles
status sources changing every cycle during a read transaction
configuration space write accesses
asynchronous reset publishes the reset register image

job.independent_model: cycle accurate job command ledger with the reset release edge detector, the sticky reported error latch and a bit counting parity reference
scenarios: reset command followed by the job done handshake
start command raises and holds running
invalid commands at both command code boundaries
command parity fault, address parity fault and both faults
back to back commands and commands separated by one and ten cycles
error capture while idle and while running, with no overwrite of the first captured word
job done publishes a zero and a non zero error word
repeat jobs after an asynchronous reset
dedicated mode constant outputs on every cycle
a reset command that arrives while an external error is asserted clears the reported error word

completion-error.independent_model: two cycle accurate lifecycle models, a completion snapshot publish acknowledge reset model and a sticky error model
scenarios: zero and non zero completion snapshots with immediate acknowledge
delayed soft reset and delayed acknowledge
completion held without acknowledge for a bounded window
single bit, simultaneous and repeated errors
a new error during publication does not replace the published word
error acknowledge immediate, delayed and absent for a bounded window
a completion and an error raised in the same cycle
both blocks frozen while disabled
asynchronous reset while idle, while pending and while publishing

mutations.expected_result: the test process exits non zero with the diagnostic of the mutated behaviour class

closed_production_findings.finding: job_out was driven by continuous assignments on cack and yield and by sequential blocks on running, done and error, so one packed structure had mixed driver kinds.
closed_production_findings.fix: The sequential state moved into job_running, job_done and job_error, and job_out is assembled by continuous assignments only. The five field cycle contract is unchanged.
closed_production_findings.evidence: The suite compiles without the BLKANDNBLK waiver, the job testbench compares running, done, error, cack and yield on every cycle, and the job-interface-constants mutation proves the constant fields are still observed.

closed_production_findings.finding: The descriptor command left payload.abt, payload.cmd.size and payload.cmd.aux_data undriven, and the whole command and request payloads were unknown before the first request. command_control consumes payload.abt as the PSL command transfer behaviour.
closed_production_findings.fix: WED_REQ now drives payload.abt, payload.cmd.size and payload.cmd.aux_data with the existing descriptor semantics, a strictly ordered 128 byte read with no auxiliary metadata, and WED_RESET clears both payloads.
closed_production_findings.evidence: The wed testbench compares the whole command payload image from the reset state onwards, and the wed-command-bus-transfer-behaviour and wed-command-tag-metadata mutations are detected.

closed_production_findings.finding: The doubleword data parity of a beat was compared against the live parity input of the following cycle while the tag parity of the same beat was compared against the value accepted with the beat, and the already latched data_write_parity_latched was dead.
closed_production_findings.fix: The comparison now uses data_write_parity_latched, the parity accepted with the beat.
closed_production_findings.evidence: afu_control latches write_valid, write_tag, write_tag_parity, write_address, write_data and write_parity of one beat into this interface in a single clocked block with one common delay, so the interface delivers every field of a beat in the same cycle. The parity-beat-association scenario counts a bin only when the accepted parity byte and the following parity byte differ, and the read-parity-beat-association mutation restores the previous expression and is detected.

closed_production_findings.finding: The beat payload registers were latched ungated while valid, tag parity and data parity were gated by the enable, so a beat accepted before an enable falling edge kept its frozen parity while the payload followed the bus, and the held valid repeated the parity compare against a fresh payload.
closed_production_findings.fix: The payload latch now resets with the block and updates only while enabled, so every field of an accepted beat freezes together.
closed_production_findings.evidence: The enabled-mid-beat-window scenarios only credit their bins when the payload presented during the window would parity differ from the frozen beat, and the read-enabled-window-payload-freeze mutation restores the ungated latch and is detected as a spurious data parity report.
